market_summary: US and Singapore markets are navigating mixed signals in early November 2026. Apple beat Q4 earnings but fell 3% after hours on weak December margin guidance (45-46% vs. 46.3% expected), as memory costs and AI spending weigh on profitability despite strong iPhone and Mac sales. Singapore's banking stocks showed divergent results: UOB reported Q3 net profit of S$1.25 billion, missing forecasts and falling 15% quarter-on-quarter on lower trading income, though fee income hit records. DBS is due to report Q3 results on November 5 with analysts expecting flat to slightly lower profit as rate compression squeezes margins. Meta raised $15 billion in bonds for AI infrastructure despite investor concerns about Big Tech's mounting AI debt. Singapore Airlines faces reputational risk from a data breach affecting 46,000 booking records via Amadeus, though no payment data was compromised.

items.headline: UOB Q3 2026 net profit S$1.25b misses forecast; record fee income cannot offset trading income decline
items.summary: <cite index="1-2,1-4">UOB's 3Q26 net profit of S$1.25 billion fell 15% quarter-on-quarter and missed the S$1.38 billion consensus forecast</cite>, though <cite index="4-6">net fee income rose 19% year-on-year to a record S$733 million, with wealth management fees at an all-time high of S$258 million</cite>. <cite index="4-2,4-5">Trading and investment income slid 33% year-on-year to S$322 million, pulling other non-interest income down 29% to S$370 million</cite>.

items.headline: DBS Q3 2026 earnings due November 5 with analysts expecting profit pressure from rate compression
items.summary: <cite index="19-8">A consensus of nine analysts polled by Visible Alpha points to third-quarter net profit of SGD 2.93 billion, down 0.7 percent from the year-earlier period</cite>. <cite index="19-4,19-5">Analysts expect fee normalization and weaker market-related income to weigh on the quarter, with investors focusing on wealth management, trading income and the bank's 2026 and 2027 outlook</cite>.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines: 46,000 booking records accessed in Amadeus data breach; no payment data exposed
items.summary: <cite index="20-4,20-5">Customer names and travel booking details from about 46,000 SIA booking records were accessed without authorisation after airline technology provider Amadeus suffered a data breach</cite>. <cite index="20-6">Amadeus confirmed to SIA that the exposed data does not include bank account or credit card information, and the unauthorised access did not result in any modification to bookings</cite>. <cite index="20-8">Other global carriers affected include Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Korean Air and Malaysia Airlines</cite>.

items.headline: Meta raises $15 billion in five-part US bond sale to fund AI infrastructure expansion
items.summary: <cite index="30-2">Meta Platforms said on Tuesday it is raising $15 billion through a five-part US dollar bond offering, as the Facebook parent turns to debt markets to help finance its accelerating investments in AI infrastructure</cite>. <cite index="31-3">Investors placed as much as $58 billion of orders on the offering, or about 3.9 times its size</cite>. <cite index="35-3">Meta's 30-year bonds are being discussed at about 2.5 percentage points above US government debt, nearly 0.9 points more than its April sale, as investors grow wary of Big Tech's AI debt</cite>.

items.headline: Apple Q4 2026 revenue $114.5B beats estimates but stock falls 3% after-hours on weak margin guidance
items.summary: <cite index="40-2,40-4">Apple posted quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent year over year, with diluted earnings per share of $2.10, up 14 percent year over year</cite>. <cite index="38-4,38-5">iPhone revenue grew 17% to $57.6 billion and Services revenue reached $31.6 billion, up 10% and reaching an all-time record</cite>. However, <cite index="45-7">the company's gross margin forecast for the December quarter is 45% to 46%, trailing the 46.3% average estimate</cite>, and <cite index="42-6">the stock fell 2.8% in after-hours trading to $328.85, as investors weighed record sales against pressure from memory costs, supply constraints and heavier spending on artificial intelligence</cite>.
